t1SeedAudit.finding: Gap confirmed and it is exactly the seeded one. SHEET-MAP-001's EARS text describes resolution as a straight alias-map lookup with an identity fallback and says nothing about the FORM of the lookup key. None of the three A-direction (spec-only) sketches independently invented input normalization — there's no textual signal that would prompt it. All three B-direction (code-only) reconstructions, by contrast, immediately surfaced the trim+upper-case normalization, because resolve_ticker's doc comment states it in prose and the new test's name names it directly. That asymmetry is the signature of B-direction elevation: forward reading under-determines the code's actual behavior; backward reading over-determines it relative to the spec. Net: code+tests assert a canonicalization contract (trim, case-fold, applied to both the alias-hit and identity-fallback paths) that the current SHEET-MAP-001 text is silent on — not contradicted, just unstated.
